SMTO-CAP-0006 — SMTO hit an internal step it doesn't recognize

GUID: 95b4169c-cbdf-4bdc-95f7-a111542d9eb6
Slug: agent-control-unknown
Domain: CAP · Subsystem: cap

What happened

  • SMTO's Agent tried an internal step that this version of SMTO doesn't know how to do, so the Task stopped there. That step didn't run, but earlier steps in the Task may have finished.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the Task and read its list of finished steps so you know what was already done before it stopped. Only this internal step was skipped; earlier steps may already have changed files or sent messages.
  2. If SMTO was updated recently, open Settings › Setup › Server updates and check the status says Server updated, not Ready to restart or Update failed. This happens when parts of SMTO come from different versions, which an unfinished update can cause.
  3. Reload the SMTO page in your browser, then send a new request for only the work that is still missing. A new request starts with the current version's steps, so the unknown step isn't used again.

What success looks like

  • The new request runs to the end without stopping on an unrecognized step.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the version shown in Server updates, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't treat the stopped Task as finished, and don't resend the original request without checking its finished steps, or done work could be repeated.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • dispatch_control reached its fallback because the requested Agent control name is not implemented by this installed runtime (Unknown agent control); the control was not executed.

What this means

  • Control dispatch reached a name not implemented by the installed Agent control handler. Capability discovery and registration describe what this run may request. They do not grant operating-system permission, override exclusions or authorize execution by themselves.

Why this can happen

  • Control dispatch reached a name not implemented by the installed Agent control handler.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the submitted control name with the current run's advertised controls and client/runtime versions.

How to fix it

  • Take the control name from the error text and compare it with the run's advertised controls (CONTROLS in src/agent_runtime/native/catalog.py) and the handlers in dispatch_control (src/agent_runtime/native/controls.py). A mismatch points to mixed runtime versions or a run resumed by a different build; finish or roll back the server update so declarations and handlers match, then start a new run for the unfinished work.
  • Use only the controls currently advertised for this run. Update an incompatible client/Skill rather than inventing a control name.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The client submits an exact supported control and receives its defined result.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass the unsupported-feature check or reinterpret an unsupported response as success.

Technical notes

  • Capability discovery and registration describe what this run may request. They do not grant operating-system permission, override exclusions or authorize execution by themselves.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
